attrs.evidence: NOT CLAIMED AND NOT TRUE IN GENERAL. The protocol removes the GLOBAL cyclic interaction — the federation carrier becomes a tree — but each super-block still has a local CSP to project, which for unrestricted Γ is NP-hard. A tree of hard problems is not an easy problem, and "efficient" must not be published on the strength of the carrier shape. Message size is likewise bounded by |D| bits only for a finite explicit sort; for a large or infinite value sort the message must be symbolic and the bit bound does not transfer. Nor is the message "the smallest" boundary summary: exactness is proved, an information-theoretic lower bound is not. SHARPENED BY THE ROUND-4 AUDIT, in the direction that makes the statement useful rather than only cautionary: for a fixed finite core template Γ, adding singleton relations/constants is polynomial-time equivalent to CSP(Γ) — a standard finite-CSP result — so the exact unary separator projection costs at most |D| satisfiability tests, one per candidate value. Hence FOR FIXED FINITE D AND A TRACTABLE CORE LANGUAGE, separator projection is tractable exactly when the local block CSP is. THE LOCAL CSP IS THE CONTROLLING TERM, not the carrier shape, and that is the correction: the question is not "does a tree carrier make this efficient". Three cautions survive. Unrestricted Γ can make the block CSP NP-hard. For a large or infinite domain, enumerating all separator values is the wrong representation and symbolic query/projection complexity is the real problem. Multi-sorted domains are handled per separator sort, AFTER computing the global core.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 round-4 audit. The singleton-relation equivalence is standard finite-CSP (Bulatov–Jeavons–Krokhin; the "conservative"/idempotent reduction).
